verses.text: At that time Jeroboam's son Abijah became sick.
Jeroboam said to his wife, "Please get up and dress up so no one will know you are my wife. Then go to Shiloh. The prophet Ahijah is there, the one who told me I would be king over this people.
Take ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey with you, and go to him. He will tell you what will happen to the boy."
Jeroboam's wife did what he said. She got up, went to Shiloh, and came to Ahijah's house. Ahijah could not see, because he had become blind in his old age.
But the LORD had told Ahijah, "Jeroboam's wife is coming to ask you about her son, because he is sick. Tell her what I tell you. When she comes, she will pretend to be someone else."
So when Ahijah heard her footsteps at the door, he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why are you pretending to be someone else? I have been sent to you with bad news.
Go and tell Jeroboam, 'This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: "I lifted you up from among the people and made you ruler over my people Israel.

I tore the kingdom away from David's family and gave it to you. But you have not been like my servant David, who kept my commands and followed me with all his heart, doing only what was right in my eyes.
You have done more evil than all who came before you. You have made yourself other gods, idols of metal, to make me angry, and you have turned your back on me.

So I am going to bring disaster on Jeroboam's family. I will cut off every male in Jeroboam's family in Israel, slave or free. I will burn up Jeroboam's family completely, as a man burns up dung until it is all gone.
Dogs will eat anyone in Jeroboam's family who dies in the city, and birds will eat those who die in the open country. The LORD has said it!"'
As for you, get up and go home. When you step into the city, the boy will die.

All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He is the only one from Jeroboam's family who will be buried in a grave, because he is the only one in that family in whom the LORD, the God of Israel, has found something good.
The LORD will raise up a king over Israel who will cut off Jeroboam's family. This is the day! Yes, even now.

The LORD will strike Israel, so that it shakes like a reed in the water. He will pull Israel up out of this good land he gave their ancestors and scatter them beyond the Euphrates River, because they made Asherah poles and made the LORD angry.
He will give Israel up because of the sins Jeroboam committed and made Israel commit."
Then Jeroboam's wife got up, left, and went to Tirzah. As soon as she stepped through the doorway of her house, the boy died.
All Israel buried him and mourned for him, just as the LORD had said through his servant the prophet Ahijah.
The rest of what Jeroboam did, how he fought and how he ruled, is written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
Jeroboam ruled for twenty-two years. Then he died, and his son Nadab became king after him.

Meanwhile, Solomon's son Rehoboam ruled in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he ruled for seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother was Naamah, an Ammonite.
The people of Judah did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. By their sins they made him more jealous than their ancestors had ever done.
They also built high places, sacred stone pillars, and Asherah poles for themselves on every high hill and under every green tree.
There were even male shrine prostitutes in the land. The people did all the disgusting things of the nations the LORD had driven out ahead of the Israelites.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam's rule, Shishak king of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.
He carried off the treasures of the LORD's temple and the treasures of the king's palace. He took everything, including all the gold shields Solomon had made.
So King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them. He gave them to the commanders of the guards who guarded the entrance to the king's palace.
Whenever the king went into the LORD's temple, the guards carried the shields, and afterward they brought them back to the guardroom.
The rest of what Rehoboam did, and all his deeds, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam the whole time.
Rehoboam died and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David. His mother was Naamah, an Ammonite. His son Abijam became king after him.
